title: Nvidia B200 Rental Prices Hit All Time High of $8.54 Per Hour
summary:
On-demand rental rates for Nvidia B200 GPUs climbed 12.9% in the past trading week amid a widespread shortage of compute capacity. Prices reached a record $8.54 per GPU-hour on the Ornn Exchange, the highest level ever tracked for the index. Nebius spot pricing for the same hardware more than tripled over the last seven days, which could help the company beat its $9B annual recurring revenue target as it annualizes December figures.

CoreWeave shares fell 25.2% during the same week that market rates rose, as 98% of the neocloud's second-quarter revenue came from committed contracts at fixed prices. Most of CoreWeave's $104B backlog is not recognized until after mid-2028, meaning current surges in on-demand pricing do not immediately benefit its existing book of business.

selectedTweets.text:
Yesterday, @OrnnExchange's B200 and B300 indexes reached a new all-time high prices, with the B200 hitting $8.54/GPU-hour.

It is clear that today's market is lacking GPU capacity, and that the companies building deploying capacity are looking to improve their credit. In the past trading week as the B200 rental price increased by 12.9%, $CRWV fell by 25.2%.

Why does $CRWV move inversely to rising compute prices as a neocloud? 98% of Coreweave's Q2 revenue came from committed contracts, 72% from three customers, and most of its $104B backlog is recognized after mid-2028.

CoreWeave's backlog is locked at fixed prices. These higher market rates matter for new contracts they sign, so the question is where rental rates end up when their contracts roll off.

Ornn's index tracks transacted prices in order to capture what buyers are actually willing to pay for on-demand GPU rentals, real signal for tracking the value of compute.
